cost.scope: Marginal Workers request and CPU only, beyond included allowances. Excludes base subscription, backend storage/requests, Foundation machine and bandwidth.
cost.samplingLimitation: Warm platform counts are adaptive estimates (41 estimated invocations from26 raw samples for48 HTTP requests), not an exact invoice or precise confidence interval.

conclusions: Public access removes customer authentication/quota work. It does not remove the Cloudflare request charge.
The current Cache API path executes Worker code on a cache hit. Positive platform invocation and CPU counters during both warm windows support the documented behavior.
CF-Cache-Status:HIT and X-Blockzilla-Cache:HIT alone cannot prove that code did not run.
Workers Cache is a documented one-Worker option that checks cached responses before executing code. It is not enabled in the current production version.
Workers Cache outer hits still pay the standard request rate. They do not consume Worker CPU.
An ordinary zone-cache origin on an existing machine could avoid Worker invocation/fee on CDN hits, but it changes routing and adds a miss hop; it remains an untested architecture option.
limitations: Cold means profile=1 Worker response/index/range cache bypass, not physically cold R2/provider caches or an empty Worker isolate. Profiling adds overhead.
Eight cold and24 warm samples per format at one Cloudflare edge; no global latency or tail percentile claim.
CPU metrics are adaptive estimates; warm counts differ from exact HTTP counts and the small-sample confidence flags are false.
Time-window script/version metrics cannot rule out unrelated external requests.
Managed Workers Cache was researched, not enabled or benchmarked. No free Workers-cache request claim is made.
